note: TECH01's bursts at a 60 ms PCR (usual 300 ms; +200/+400 ramped at 101/102 s for 12 s, -200 for 11 s, every 150 s), the window rule holding the line at the bursts' height from the first step (111.3 s); at 600 s the source timeline (PCR and PES) jumps forward by 1000 ms with no discontinuity flag (chapter 15.4 B-95). The leap relock (600.3 s) re-seeds the line on the next sample at the usual level, so the held excess is dropped once per PID at that switch (360.0 / 362.7 ms at 600.67 s); the next burst steps again (711.3 s) and the line is held again. Before B-95 the pairs instead (13 relocks, 12 overlaps 6.81 s) and nothing dropped at the jump (a 5.3 ms epoch gap per PID: that line sat at the usual level). The drop at the jump is the price of the held line, by design: the new line is the source's new timeline, seeded as every leap epoch is, so this pins the consequence.
